newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO to buy Britain's Causeway Group.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO to buy Britain's Causeway Group.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Monday it had reached agreement to buy British funds manager Causeway Group Ltd for an undisclosed sum.
The Causeway funds, which provide development capital to the British quoted and unquoted sectors, have been subscribed by more than 80 institutions from Britain and the United States.
Funds under management have grown to about 300 million stg today from 10 million stg when first funds were raised in 1984.
The purchase is being through ABN AMRO's securities network, ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.

ABN AMRO said the directors of Causeway decided to sell all of its issued capital as a change of control was inevitable with the planned retirement next year of major shareholder and founding director, David Secker Walker, at the age of 65.
Causeway, to be renamed ABN AMRO Causeway, will continue its activities and pursue expansion with the current management team, led by the other founding director, Lionel Anthony.
It will operate within ABN AMRO Hoare Govett UK, part of the group's global investment banking network.
ABN AMRO said this would enable Causeway to continue its strong growth in managing equity finance for quoted and unquoted companies.
"Causeway will be the platform for building ABN AMRO's private equity business in the UK and will operate closely with the bank's global private equity network," ABN AMRO said.

Anthony said in a statement Causway's new parent company intended to assist future fund raising and support it with new products, including debt and equity finance, related to the development capital market.
